newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain rejects Amnesty's trial criticism.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain rejects Amnesty's trial criticism.

text.p: Bahrain on Tuesday rejected criticism from the human rights group Amnesty International over the trial of 81 people accused of involvement in what officials termed a pro-Iranian plot to topple the government.
A justice ministry official quoted by Bahrain's official Gulf News Agency rejected charges by the London-based human rights group that the suspects were not getting a fair trial.
"The right to a fair trial, defence and guarantees in accordance with Bahrain's laws were made available," the Gulf Arab state's official said.
He said the defendants were being tried by the State Security Court "with the presence of their lawyers and their families".
"The suspects are being tried for committing crimes according to Bahrain's penal code issued in 1976," the official said.
Amnesty claimed the trial was grossly unfair, with none of the defendants having the right to appeal before a higher court.
It said most trial sessions for the suspects -- 59 people in court and the rest tried in absentia -- had been closed to the public and no independent observers were allowed to attend.
The Bahraini justice official said: "Lawyers defending them are allowed to study the cases, charges and confessions by the suspects...There is nothing suspicious in the current trial."
Lawyers said on Tuesday the court, which began hearing the case on March 1, would soon pass its verdicts. Some suspects could face the death penalty if convicted.
The court, whose judgement cannot be appealed, was set up by the government in March 1996 to speed up rulings. It said this week that final defence statements would be given on Wednesday.

The defendants are accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and having contacts with a foreign country.
Political parties are banned in Bahrain. Bahrain in June accused Iran of backing an attempt to overthrow the government. Iran denied the charge.

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community seeking political and economic reform by the Sunni rulers, have waged a campaign of bombings, arson, sabotage and riots since December 1994. At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested.
